summary: In Greek mythology, Arsinoe (Ancient Greek Ἀρσινόη) is a name borne by several women. The atlas node arsinoe-psophis is the daughter of Phegeus of Psophis — also called Alphesiboea — first wife of Alcmaeon, who receives Harmonia's necklace and robe and is later enslaved at Tegea after condemning her brothers for her husband's murder.

sections.heading: Wife of Alcmaeon
paragraphs: After Alcmaeon is purified by Phegeus for killing Eriphyle, he marries Arsinoe and deposits with her the cursed necklace and robe of Harmonia. When he later seeks a second purification and a new wife, Phegeus' sons Pronous and Agenor kill him; Arsinoe condemns the murder and is shut in a chest, carried to Tegea, and given as a slave to Agapenor under a false charge.

Homonym guard: not Arsinoe daughter of Leucippus (Messenian mother of Asclepius in the rival tradition); not the Nysiad nurse of Dionysus; not Orestes' nurse. The atlas id is Phegeus' daughter of Psophis alone.
